Greek Kings.
that they might come to their aid and surrender to the fortress.
The king, however, hastened, went, and encamped against the fortress;
and the Armenians who were inside seized the Greek magnates,
and surrendered them to the king,
and they destroyed (or: he destroyed?) all of them.
He also destroyed Bahram in the fortress of the city of Anazarba.
For when they had fled to that fortress,
the king sent the Greek Patriarch of Antioch to them and swore:
"If they come down in peace,
I will not harm them."
Now that patriarch, when he went to them, said to them:
"Do not come down,
lest he destroy you all."
And he returned, came, and said to him:
"They did not listen to me to come down."
And the king perceived what had been done by him.
And when he had destroyed those men,
he seized the patriarch to send him to the King of Constantinople,
so that he might judge between them.
Now that patriarch, when he was delivered by the king to the soldiers to take him to Constantinople,
his conductors took him and brought him to the city of Ayas,
and pitched a tent for him by the seashore.
And when they entered the city to buy provisions for themselves,
they were also preoccupied with drinking wine until night.
The patriarch sent to some Greek sailors who happened to be nearby,
and called them to him,
and wept before them,
and showed them:
"It is to destroy him,
and not to take him to Constantinople,
that the Armenians are putting him into the sea."
And when they were grieved for him,
they snatched him away in their small boat,
and brought him to the territory of the Romans, to the Turks.
At this time,
Leo, king of the Armenians, gave his daughter, the one by a concubine, to the son of the Parwana,
instead of his sister whom his father had not given him;
and a somewhat borrowed reconciliation took place between them.
And in the year 1584 [A.G.],
{there was an earthquake in the} cities of Azerbaijan,
and especially in the city of Tabriz.
And it demolished courtyards and mosques,
and the tops of towers fell.
Our church, however,
the Lord preserved without shaking,
and the service did not cease from it, while Greeks, Armenians, Nestorians, and all of our own people were gathering in it.
